entries.alt: Jesus watches beside a man who holds up and examines his restored hand in a synagogue.
findings: Head inclination changed, but Christ's pupils still appear up/right beyond the bowed man's eye line. They do not clearly settle on his face or restored hand.
Approved identity, quiet expression, man's hand and synagogue composition remain credible.
entries.action: Aim Christ's eyes visibly down-right at the raised restored hand; preserve the man's gaze at that hand. Do not import this revision.

entries.alt: Jesus listens to two men on a village street, meeting the central messenger's gaze as the man gestures.
entries.caption: Friends bring the centurion's message to Jesus. Luke places the conversation with these messengers, while the centurion expresses trust in the authority of Jesus' word.
findings: Christ's head and visible pupils now turn right/down toward the central messenger's eyes. The messenger looks up to Him; attention is reciprocal.
Canonical identity, natural listening expression, hands and secondary faces remain coherent.

entries.alt: Jesus and a seated scribe face one another in conversation as the scribe gestures with an open hand.
entries.caption: Jesus and a scribe discuss love for God and neighbor. Their attentive exchange illustrates the conversation recorded in Mark, with the setting and poses imagined.
findings: Lowered head and eyes now align with the scribe's eyes. The former upward look over him is corrected.
Canonical likeness, attentive expression, hands, scroll and distinct secondary figures are preserved.
